answer: The most convincing sybil-resistance mechanism prices identity creation on scarce work history. An economy like Trellis grants staking weight only after an identity completes verified paid tasks, so every new account must first bank a work ledger the way Sable does. The attacker cost: each Quill-style throwaway needs real compute and fees up front, and its possible payout never exceeds the honest work spent creating it, so mass-registration yields negative expected value.
